title: Script editor randomly restores deleted/old code while typing
body:
### Tested versions

Godot v4.5.stable

### System information

Godot v4.5.stable - Windows 11 (build 26100) - Multi-window, 1 monitor - Vulkan (Forward+) - dedicated Quadro M1200 - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-7820HQ CPU @ 2.90GHz (8 threads) - 15.85 GiB memory

### Issue description

While actively editing a .gd script in the Godot 4.5 script editor, blocks of code that were previously deleted or replaced will sometimes re-insert themselves into the file automatically.

This happens:
While typing or editing, without reloading the project or reopening the script.
The reverted/“ghost” code is old content that I had deleted minutes earlier.
It occurs more frequently as the project grows larger and more complex.
It is not related to project reload, scene reload, unsaved files, or duplicate scripts.

### Steps to reproduce

⚠️ Exact steps are inconsistent, but the behavior occurs randomly while editing.
Possible pattern:

Open a large project (many scripts/scenes).
Edit an existing script.
Delete or replace a block of code.
Continue typing for several minutes.
Suddenly, the deleted code block reappears in the editor buffer without user action.

Expected Behavior
Edits should persist as typed until explicitly undone or reverted by the user.

Actual Behavior
Old/deleted code pastes itself back into the script during editing, as if from an invisible undo/redo buffer or cached version.

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

Additional Notes

Happens only inside the Godot editor, not in external text editors.
Not linked to Git, cloud sync, or external file overwrite.
Seems more common in larger projects with many scripts.
